:::{.theorem data-title="Closed Sets & Convergent Sequences"}

For
[[knowledge-mathematics-analysis-functional-analysis-metric-spaces|metric space]]
$(X,d)$ a subset $A\subseteq X$ is
[[open-sets-closed-sets-on-metric-spaces|closed]] iff for every
[[sequence-convergence|convergent sequence]]
$\{a_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subseteq A$ one has
$\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}a_{n}\in A$.

:::

`\begin{proof}`
We construct a proof by contraposition. Assume that $A\subseteq X$ is open
which implies that $A^c$ is closed. Therefore, there is a limit point
$x\in A^c$ such that $B_\epsilon(x)\cap A\neq \emptyset$ for all $\epsilon>0$.
`\end{proof}`
